#1536. Andoni Iraola has Liverpool's fearsome frontline firing, Alexis Mac Allister back to his best and is unlocking the best of Florian Wirtz... it is far too soon to count them out of the title race, writes LEWIS STEELE

Published: 22:00 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 08:57 EDT, 1 November 2026

Are Liverpool in the title race? The question has been bandied around this week — and conversations will only grow louder if they beat Arsenal at Anfield tomorrow.

The clash feels like an early six-pointer but regardless of the result, we can make this point — Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool are on the up and, whether this year or next, will soon be competing for the top prizes again.

This follows a season of strife in which the football was boring, the title defence fell apart and fans turned mutinous — booing, leaving early and moaning at manager Arne Slot.

The Dutchman paid with his job and in came Iraola, who — with respect to Bournemouth and Rayo Vallecano — had no experience of managing the day-to-day stresses and demands of a club of this size.

Three months into his reign, the Basque is yet to receive the plaudits he deserves. Maybe because Arsenal are champions and the two Manchester clubs are never out of the headlines, Liverpool have gone under the radar.

But they have lost just once, when down to 10 men against Manchester City, and have won their last five games, including some potential banana skins. So is it time to stop sleeping on this team’s chances?

Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool are on the up and will soon be competing for the top prizes again

Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola are starting to fire for Iraola

We can go position by position and analyse how the Reds have improved under Iraola. In attack, there was a potential narrative of a post-Mohamed Salah slump, but the absence of the Egyptian has rarely been mentioned.

In the summer, Iraola said he wants his forwards to be ‘game changers’ and he has plenty of those — Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Rio Ngumoha have all fulfilled that role, plus Hugo Ekitike when he returns from injury.

In midfield, Alexis Mac Allister is back to his best and Iraola sees the Argentine as his coach on the pitch, a man who reads the game better than anyone. Wirtz is getting better while young Trey Nyoni, 19, has been outstanding when he has featured.

At the back, Jeremy Jacquet has been a revelation. Fellow new signing Ronald Araujo is only on loan from Barcelona — there is an option to make that permanent — but is becoming a cult hero.

Iraola has also got the fans back on side. It is fair to say the Kop was unsure of him when he arrived but he has won them over with a front-footed, exciting style in a system that demands hard work and relentless pressing.

There is the perfect blend of youth and experience and it is clear the team are fighting for one another again.

‘It’s not just winning,’ Iraola said. ‘At Anfield, everyone feels when the team goes for it and when everyone is giving everything, trying his best… then the supporters will be there. Even when we have been losing, they have helped us massively.’

Florian Wirtz endured a difficult first season at Anfield but is starting to show why the club paid big money to sign him from Bayer Leverkusen in 2025

Jeremy Jacquet has been a revelation in the Liverpool defence

Captain Virgil van Dijk added: ‘The fans definitely like what they’re seeing and, of course, you feel that energy and it’s great. I’ve been feeling that energy for quite a while and when you miss it then to get it back is obviously very good.’

So, title race? Absolutely. Beat Arsenal and they are only three points behind the Gunners, so why not? Lose and it is nine points, which would not be insurmountable with 29 games and six months to go, but would certainly reduce the margin for error.

Usurping the Gunners might be a step too far this season, but Liverpool are certainly stronger than last term — and Iraola says there is still plenty of room for improvement.

Just look at his Bournemouth side. Winless in their first nine games, they barely looked back as they qualified for Europe. Liverpool had a rocky first month with obvious deficiencies, but are now building a head of steam.

Arsenal visit on Sunday having not won at Anfield since 2012 - last season this fixture was won by Dominik Szoboszlai's stunning 35-yard free-kick

The small details are also improving, such as solidity from set-pieces — an issue that bugged them last term with a league-high 20 goals conceded. The fitness of Isak is a huge factor, while Alisson looks in top condition again.

Asked where his team can improve, Iraola said: ‘Almost everywhere. We are defending really well lately but still we have some situations where we need to improve. In the league, we have been less dangerous offensively.

‘So it is still too early to make big conclusions but there are improvements needed everywhere.’

Arsenal might not be wary of Manchester City given potential points deductions but, should Liverpool beat them on Halloween weekend, the champions will certainly be running scared.

#1535. Man United: Yoro’s terrible mistake against Bournemouth

Starting in the Manchester United defense this Sunday at Old Trafford, Leny Yoro completely missed his intervention by sliding on the left side of his area, leaving Bournemouth to take advantage of the offering. Truffert immediately recovered the ball before serving Tavernier, completely alone against Lammens.

The Bournemouth winger did not tremble to adjust the Belgian goalkeeper on his left and allow the Cherries to make the break. A big individual error for Yoro, who weighs down the Red Devils a little more in an already complicated period. Manchester United is sinking into crisis and its young defender risks thinking about this slide for a long time.

#1534. Why you can't blame Aston Villa chiefs for fighting back at Jamie Carragher as Fulham refuse to follow pundit in backing down as they earn deserved point, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

Published: 18:11 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 09:34 EDT, 1 November 2026

Aston Villa might have had an apology from Jamie Carragher but Unai Emery’s men found Fulham far more awkward opponents on a difficult night at Villa Park.

After Villa had threatened legal action, the Sky Sports pundit said sorry for telling ‘Aston Villa fans’ to ‘shut the f*** up’ on Saturday. The Holte End let Carragher know what they thought of him within a minute here.

Unfortunately for Villa, Fulham were in no mood to back down as Carragher had. John McGinn missed a penalty for the home side early on and though Nicolas Jackson gave them a half-time lead, Fulham deservedly equalised when Zion Suzuki – outstanding until then – carried Alex Iwobi’s corner over his own line.

Though Villa were very poor in the second half, this remains a team in transition and there will be bumps in the road. And thanks to the dispute with Carragher, the main talking point on Saturday was away from the pitch.

Villa have been mocked for this response but look at it from their point of view. The club feel that at every turn, the established order are trying to slow their progress.

Consider the financial regulations that favour historically wealthy clubs who make money off the pitch, over those who have started to succeed on it.

Nicolas Jackson has been on fire this season and netted again to give Villa the lead

Villa would certainly have settled for Champions League fixture pile-ups 10 years ago

Imagine the frustration of finishing fourth in the Premier League, winning the Europa League and then having to sell six starters from the Final.

Now he has to listen to ex-players with significant influence telling the world that Villa can never satisfy Emery’s ambition.

Carragher is probably guilty of nothing more than expressing an opinion, however crudely he may have done so. But if Sawiris is fed up of various voices and organisations trying to put Villa back in their box, who can blame him?

Whenever Antonee Robinson charged down the Fulham left, Villa were in trouble. The US international had a superb match but until his error, the visitors found Suzuki in excellent form.

He made one outstanding stop from Oscar Bobb and produced decisive interventions to deny Gonzalo Garcia, Josh King and Alex Iwobi.

There is plenty of technical ability in this side and when they move forward they are great to watch. But Garcia does not look a ruthless finisher in the style of Jackson and he missed chances here. At the back, too, they look flimsy. As well as Jackson took his goal, the challenges from Timothy Castagne and David Affengruber were weak.

Yet in Josh King and Oscar Bobb they have twinkle-toed attackers capable of threatening any defence. After a poor start to his tenure, it looks as though Alvaro Arbeloa is starting to find his range at Craven Cottage and had they won here, it would have been fully merited.

Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki got into a terrible mess to gift Fulham an equaliser

Villa would certainly have settled for Champions League fixture pile-ups ten years ago, when they were eking out a 1-1 draw at rivals Birmingham in the Championship, but their recent schedule has been unforgiving.

With Villa facing Barca at the Nou Camp on Tuesday, the Fulham game was brought forward from 2pm on Sunday to the late fixture on Saturday. That is exactly 72 hours after the Carabao Cup defeat to Bournemouth, and 72 before they face the Spanish champions.

Given Villa made several changes at Bournemouth, surely there was a case making this a 12.30pm kick-off, or even a 3pm kick-off on Saturday? Given the short turnaround before facing one of Europe’s strongest sides, Villa will be glad to have won their opening three games.

That gives them a clear shot at the last 16, either by qualifying directly or through the play-offs. Barcelona also opted not to rest players and fielded a strong side against Alaves in La Liga on Saturday, which was also an 8pm kick-off.

The bad news is that Hansi Flick’s side were 4-0 up at half-time and went on to win 6-1. If Fulham were able to cause Villa this much trouble with sharp passing and movement, what about the club most associated with those qualities?

Emery and his squad will certainly travel to Barcelona a little nervously on Monday afternoon.

#1532. Ranking the 10 best attacking midfielders in world football: Fernandes falls, and just how good is Nico Paz?

Who are the best attacking midfielders in world football right now? It’s a stacked field, with creative stars from Real Madrid, Manchester United, Manchester City and Chelsea amongst the best in Europe at this moment.

Before we begin, a quick clarification. This list is exclusively for No.10s, playmakers and attack-minded midfielders. Deeper operators, holding midfielders and box-to-box No.8s can be found elsewhere, even if some regularly chip in with goals and assists.

With that out of the way, here’s our ranking of the 10 best attacking midfielders in world football.

Morgan Rogers takes 10th place after grabbing his big-money move to Chelsea by the scruff of the neck. The Blues remain a work in progress under Xabi Alonso, but it helps enormously that Rogers has hit the ground running after an eye-watering transfer fee.

Morgan Gibbs-White drops out after failing to maintain the exceptional form he showed in the latter half of last season. Florian Wirtz goes too. We’ve been waiting for the penny to drop for months, and are finally admitting defeat.

Honourable mentions for Johan Manzambi, who has hit the ground running at Villa, and Julio Enciso, one of our favourite players to watch in the Premier League right now. They could push for inclusion if they can keep up this form.

Another player that wasn’t at his best last season, with his omission from the England squad the price for that.

Really it’s been diminishing returns since his incredible debut season at Chelsea, arguably the most exciting campaign from a young English player since Dele Alli burst onto the scene a decade ago. Apologies in advance if we’ve just hexed him with that comparison.

There have been flashes of the old Palmer in 2026-27, not least in the wins over Fulham, Leeds and Manchester United. But inconsistency remains an issue, with some quieter displays preventing us from declaring a full-blown revival.

The talent remains unquestionable, and a fit, confident Palmer still walks into almost any team in Europe. We just want to see him put a proper run together again.

Olmo leaves us with this minor sense of frustration that he’s not quite what he should or could be. Maybe we’re just too demanding of our continental creators.

You wouldn’t necessarily put him among Barcelona’s five most important players, but he’s a nice fit in this free-scoring side and invariably makes things happen when available. There have been some lovely moments in 2026-27, but the familiar fitness issues persist.

We’re still waiting for him to put together a sustained run of form. Flick and Luis de la Fuente clearly know what they’ve got, and we’re inclined to trust their judgement.

Lopez is far from the biggest star in Barcelona’s team, but the La Masia graduate is proving quite the asset. Chelsea’s reported €40million bid looks hilariously cheeky in hindsight.

He’s made an excellent start to 2026-27, with six goals and seven assists, while his relentless energy and commitment make him particularly well-suited to Hansi Flick’s all-action gameplan.

There are still small question marks over whether he can consistently deliver in the very biggest games, but he’s gradually answering those doubts. He’s now just about ahead of Dani Olmo in our estimation.

We shouldn’t forget what Fernandes did for Manchester United last season. His individual campaign was comfortably the best of any player in his position across world football. But even at his best, there have always been awkward questions about whether such a traditional No.10 can exist in a proper team.

Think Philippe Coutinho at Liverpool back in the day, or later-day Mesut Ozil at Arsenal.

United’s dreadful start to 2026-27 has only brought those concerns back into focus. Fernandes has hardly covered himself in glory, with the whingeing, flouncing and erratic pressing hardly setting the example you’d expect of a captain.

He’s still got plenty of fight, as demonstrated by his fiery interview after the much-needed comeback against Roma. But if United are serious about building something different, perhaps January is the time to call it a day. There’s a Saudi-shaped solution staring everyone in the face.

READ: Ranking the 10 best midfielders in world football: Rodri, Rice, Vitinha…

Cherki remains one of the most beautifully watchable footballers in the game. He’s capable of moments of outright genius, the sort of player who makes you wonder why everyone doesn’t try a little harder to entertain us.

But perhaps there’s a boring reason why throwback players of his ilk are becoming increasingly rare in elite football. The demands of modern pressing, positional discipline and collective responsibility don’t always leave much room for a player who wants to do things his own way.

It’s been a familiar mixture of ups and downs under Maresca in 2026-27, with the occasional flash of brilliance offset by the inevitable tactical friction. We’re still intrigued.

He’s no Luka Modric, but Guler is probably the closest thing Real Madrid have to the legendary Croatian these days. A more advanced, attack-minded version, admittedly, but one capable of taking control of a game.

Rather than forcing him out wide, the Madrid manager has found a structure that allows Guler to help dictate tempo while Bellingham operates in his favoured central role. It’s working well.

Guler possesses bags of creativity, with his dead-ball deliveries an especially valuable asset. He was instrumental in the comeback against Roma and held his own in their statement Clasico win.

Odegaard doesn’t quite offer the creative output of Fernandes or the individual flair of Cherki. But there’s a reason Mikel Arteta loves him. Do you really think the Arsenal manager would swap him for either?

He’s the embodiment of the champions. Disciplined, hard-working, positionally intelligent and willing to sacrifice individual glory for the collective. Unlikely to be loved by neutrals, but why should he care if he’s captaining the best side in the country?

Last season wasn’t his finest, with a noticeable decline in his attacking output, but the early signs in 2026-27 are considerably more encouraging. He’s already doubled his league goal tally from last season.

We wondered whether we’d been getting a little carried away by putting Paz as high as third in this ranking over the summer. A key player for Como, certainly, but he barely featured at the World Cup. Were we perhaps overegging the pudding?

Turns out we were right to have faith. The Argentinian has taken to bigger tests like a duck to water, looking absolutely resplendent in Como’s 4-1 mauling of Manchester United before earning a perfect 10 WhoScored rating with a goal and two assists in their 9-1 tonking of Lens.

He’s a ridiculous footballer, and we’re bumping him up accordingly. The epitome of the modern No.10, Paz combines individual brilliance with the tactical intelligence and work rate to thrive in a sophisticated pressing system.

Argentina’s great hope now that Messi has retired. We can’t wait to see what the future holds.

For two straight seasons, Bellingham didn’t quite hit the heights expected of him. No major trophies. Fairly modest numbers. Questions over how he fits alongside Real Madrid’s other stars. And a growing sense of frustration amid the club’s wider issues.

It’s been a similar story for Kylian Mbappe, with the pair taking their time to develop an understanding at the Bernabeu.

But the World Cup offered a pretty clear explanation: the problem isn’t Bellingham or Mbappe. It’s Madrid. More specifically, it’s a midfield that still hasn’t adequately replaced Toni Kroos and Luka Modric.

But finally, things are starting to click. Bellingham is now consistently operating in a role that suits him, rather than being shoehorned into a deeper midfield position he can’t really play, and is once again one of Madrid’s most important players, regularly contributing big moments.

This was the same player who was a genuine Ballon d’Or contender a couple of years ago, driving Madrid to a Champions League and La Liga double. He hasn’t changed.

#1531. Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under big pressure

This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

But then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

United were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent big players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

They hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

The question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s new head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

There was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL

And the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

Patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the issue then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

United can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

“We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

Even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

The decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but big moments in games like that have a big impact.

We did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game. We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

We could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have. That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to wining ways.

The red card changed the plan of the game but credit to the players because the effort, spirit and togetherness has been brilliant.

[On Foden’s red card] Can be a red card, but in the same action can be a red card for Bruno. It is what it is, we won.

Changed the plan for us, and changed the plan for them. They are unbelievable in transition, and the moment we are with 10 men we give them no transitions.

When you are able to win a game with 10 players it’s fantastic, when this game is a derby it’s even better.

Last year with Chelsea I had a player sent off here after three minutes, this year 25, hopefully next time we play against 11vs11!

We always knew it was going to be a tough game. What happened with Phil at the start wasn’t good for us, but we said at half-time it would make us feel better if we win and we’ve taken three points.

It just gives you more motivation to go on and get the points. It was really tough for us. We had to run more and fight more. We all shone, to a man, and we were brilliant.

He was offside and what I can’t understand is it’s the rules... I went there because he was in front of him because that’s why Haaland was free at the back.

Every season they come to our club and spend an hour and a half explaining the rules, and they seem so confident with that, and then you have five or six people making this mistake. It’s unacceptable.

Haaland speaking on Sky: “We had to go low which is not ideal, we like to keep the ball, to try to score goals but in these times you have to go a bit low and take your chances when possible. We managed to do that well and that shows personality and character, to keep the ball away at Old Trafford with 10 men.”

“We had to change the plan a bit, but Enzo gave us a plan where we could play to our different strengths and counter-attack a bit more. For me personally, I just had to be there, to try to wait for a chance, and if there’s a chance, I had to be ready to execute. We also needed fighters in the team, which we have plenty of. Look at our midfield - it’s something they like to do! I’m so, so proud of everyone.”

And on Donnarumma’s late save: “This wolf in goal giving you so much confidence, he looks a bit like a wolf. He is a mad man but he is a match-winner as well.”

9 - Erling Haaland is now the top scorer in Premier League games between Manchester City and Manchester United:9 - Haaland (8 apps)8 - Agüero (13 apps)8 - Rooney (21 apps)Domination. pic.twitter.com/EBiifV12st

City win the Old Trafford derby with 10 men and Enzo Maresca runs down the touchline to celebrate in front of the travelling fans while their players embrace Donnarumma after his late save.

There will be so much analysis of Foden’s red card, but more so how Haaland’s winner stood given the final result. Should Enzo Fernandez have been considered offside?

But if you are judging performances, City are worthy winners. They defended stoutly, carried a threat and kept the ball well for periods even though they were a man light. United were aimless and froze.

A mammoth victory, and one which perhaps puts the breaks on talk of an Arsenal procession.

What a chance for Mbeumo to equalise! Superb save by Donnarumma, after the United forward was found by a Bruno Fernandes disguised pass into the box. Mbeumo took the ball under his spell and shot with power, but the big goalkeeper pushed the shot over the bar.

United have a corner, but Michael Oliver blows for a foul, and that is surely that.

Martinez tries a straight ball towards Sesko, which is too high for the striker. United have perhaps just one more attack in them if they are too salvage a point.

Dalot with another poor cross that flies over everyone in the penalty area. Then Mainoo’s pass in midfield is intercepted by Anderson, and Ndiaye can bring the ball forward for City until he his tackled buy Martinez.

Fernandes drifts a cross behind for a City goal kick, between Sesko and Zirkzee and it looks like United are running out of time and ideas.

Dorgu with another foul on Ndiaye, yet another break in play for City. And there are going to just FIVE minutes of added time, much to Old Trafford’s frustration.

Haaland does well to bring City forward after another United attack breaks down, and Dorgu is penalised for a foul on Ndiaye. Another stoppage follows because the ball hits Michael Oliver. City can see the finish line so, and they would deserve their three points.

United have a corner after Guehi stands firm to block Cunha’s strike from distance. Maguire rises highest in the middle, but no United player gambled on the knockdown and his header drifts wide of the post.

Good work from Anderson against Mainoo in midfield, he receives a big cheer from the City fans. Carrick has thrown attackers on, but United have lost some structure and are not sustaining pressure.

Nico O’Reilly is now on for the closing stages, in place of Fernandez and Carrick has thrown on Zirkzee in place of Marcus Rashford. A United goal now would feel like a goal out of nowhere. City are playing the better football now and they have a corner.

United have lost all sense of momentum, City are keeping the ball for spells and then are happy for the game to be broken up stoppages.

Fernandez goes down looking for a penalty rather hopefully, and Maguire has been booked for his reaction as well as Fernandez for his role in the fracas. More and more time ticks away.

City are showing real resolve as well as quality here, Enzo Fernandez has just won a free-kick in the United half after a foul by Mainoo. The closest United have come in recent minutes was a glancing header wide from Mbeumo.

From that free-kick, Fernandez’s low delivery is close to being converted by Haaland or Guehi.

It’s a big final 16 minutes here plus injuries for United. You’re at home to your derby rivals who have been down to 10 men since the 23rd minute and you’ve had just two players show up for the mostpart so far - Mainoo and Rashford. The rest are really going to have to lift it.

Fernandes stings the palms of Donnarumma with a strike from outside the box.

We have now had an explanation and evidence of why the goal stood. The VAR check for offside on Haaland found that he was in fact onside by fine margins, and that Fernandez (who was offside) did not affect Lisandro Martinez as he threw himself at a diving header (and missed). The Fernandez element feels the more debatable.

#MUNMCI – 59' VAR OVERTURNVAR checked the referee's call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded.The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn't play the ball. pic.twitter.com/TyTip3ACIh

Enzo Fernandes’s shot from the edge of the D is tipped on to the post by Lammens! United are living dangerously, and Carrick has now thrown Sesko on in place of Tielemans.

Sesko on for United. Surprised he’s not come on before. City fans singing “Enzo, he’s in your head, Enzo, Enzo” to the tune of the Cranberries’ Zombie – and then he goes and hits a post.

What a final 30 minutes or so of football we have in store now. There will be an air of panic spreading through the United ranks, and Haaland, Ndiaye and Semenyo are still posing a threat.

Haaland and his City team-mates run off to celebrate in front of the away fans including Noel Gallagher.

The goalscorer looked marginally ahead of Dorgu and offside, but the camera angles can deceive. The reasoning for the final decision is not entirely clear.

United fans were goading and laughing at their City counterparts when the goal was initially ruled out for offside but it’s City who have had the last laugh.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

Sky are saying that VAR has concluded the striker is in an “onside position”.

It looks like they might be checking the position of Enzo Fernandez in the middle.

Haaland has the ball in the net but the flag is up for offside! Great finish at the back post from Gvardiol’s cross, but the City striker had just strayed offside. There is an ongoing VAR check, though.

City with a better sequence of passing but it does Ndiaye cannot get a shot away and then Fernandez commits another foul in midfield. Cunha with a poor cross behind for a City goal kick.

Bryan Mbeumo with a wild shot over the bar after cutting inside from the right, Mainoo was involved in propelling United forward once again. Then Cunha shoots over from a tight angle, but United are knocking on the door now.

Much better from United in the last few minutes, the crowd are engaged again and possibly for the first time in the game it feels like a goal might be coming. Nice idea from Rashford to let the ball run to Dorgu but the left-back is offside.

Kobbie Mainoo hits the post! Lovely strike from 25 yards after a Dalot pull-back is flicked into his path by Fernandes. Plenty of whip on it, and Donnarumma was beaten all ends up. Then United are back at the heart of the City defence, but Rashford’s shot deflects behind for a corner, from which the City goalkeeper is fouled.

He’s been United’s best player by a distance so far this season and Kobbie Mainoo goes very close there to giving United the lead with a fine strike that hits the post. Next passage of play and he releases Rashford in on the left whose shot is pushed out for a corner.

Haaland does well to win City a free-kick in the United half after rolling Martinez. City had an early United corner to defend but they did so well. Quite a slow tempo to the game all round.

Fernandez’s deep delivery finds the unmarked Dias, and his header deflects behind for a City corner. Maguire heads away, and then Anderson’s cross drifts behind for a goal kick.

Strange moment as the game kicks-off while Sky’s Patrick Davison is still talking to Michael Carrick. He signs off in almost apologetic fashion for distracting the United manager from his job.

Ndiaye on for Cherki, so Maresca opting for a player who can dribble the ball over long distances.

Keane said: “For me, Fernandes is the player who has been violent. I don’t think that is a red card for Foden. Foden is a bit daft, but so is Bruno.”

This fixture has often brought out the best in Phil Foden but this is a third successive visit to Old Trafford he will want to forget. He was substituted at half-time of the 2-0 defeat in January with a broken hand and the season before he had been withdrawn before the hour mark after a poor performance in a 0-0 draw. And now sent off after 24 minutes.

A half that will be remembered for one thing and one thing only: Phil Foden’s red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

United were shading things before that flashpoint, but City will be pleased with their response to the sending off. They have defended well, and posed a threat going forward without executing the final pass or shot.

This is now a different game to the one United were expecting, so perhaps Carrick needs to shuffle the pack.

United win a free-kick about 25 yards from goal after Enzo Fernandez chases his own poor touch and fouls Tielemans.

Rashford to take... cracking hit, up and over the wall but the attempt bounces wide off the post.

United struggling to carve out clear openings, nobody was planning for the game to have this pattern with the home team dominating possession and City dropping off into a deep defensive shape. Nunes does exceptionally well to win a tackle, drive out from the back and find Cherki.

City threaten again after a poor defensive header by Dalot, with Semenyo fizzing in a low cross that is deflected behind for a corner with Fernandez lurking in the six-yard box. United have lost their way in the last 10 minutes, Dalot flagged offside unnecessarily.

There’s a reminder of City’s threat: Haaland spinning a pass wide right to Cherki who is in acres, but with Haaland in the middle and Semenyo on the edge of the box he crosses to nobody at the back stick.

He was not a starter in Carrick’s original game plan, but I wonder if United’s task now calls for Benjamin Sesko and some extra penalty-box presence and aerial threat. Guehi is having a very sound game at the back for City.

Both teams adjusting after the red card, Cherki and Semenyo are trying to put in a defensive shift in front of their full-backs. United enjoying the majority of possession, and Fernandes feeds Rashford with a delightful reverse pass but Rashford’s first touch was loose.

United will now be favourites to win this game, but Mainoo was required to block a goal-bound strike from Cherki after a corner was clear. City do have the ammunition to offer a threat on the break. They need the Haaland of his Dortmund days to attack big spaces on the counter.

Old Trafford is delirious because United’s scourge in so many derbies is off for an early shower. Fernandes and Foden were scrapping for the ball near the touchline, the United man had a nibble at Foden as he tried to protect the ball. But then Foden kicked up from the ground with his studs into the midriff of Fernandes. I don’t think he can have any complaints.

There are plenty of players on show, on both sides ,who will hope to be in contention including Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford for United although Harry Maguire may have talked his way out of being considered after his reaction to not making the World Cup squad. For City there is Marc Guehi and Elliot Anderson - who both will be included - and it feels like a big game for Phil Foden.

Very wasteful from Haaland, after Bruno Fernandes’s stray wall pass back into midfield ran into his path. Neither picked a pass nor let fly with a shot and lost control of the ball.

At the other end, Guehi defends well against Rashford and City have a goal kick, but United have the upper hand in the game at the moment.

Cunha with a burst through City’s midfield and he is brought down by Fernandez. Mainoo then whips a teasing cross to the back post, but Rashford misread the flight of it and he was offside in any case.

City with a more sustained spell of possession in the United half, but Martinez defends well as Foden dribbles into the penalty area. Cunha then tries to release Rashford behind the City defence, but Dias covered well behind Guehi to intercept.

Promising counter-attack for United after Rashford pinches the ball off Foden in midfield, and the home team’s attacking quartet of players stream forward. Poor from Cunha though, dragging a shot well wide from an improbable distance.

Quite a composed start from City, Anderson enjoying plenty of touches in midfield. Fernandes tries to sweep a first-time pass out to Rashford wide left, but Nunes intercepts.

Then Fernandes’s next pass is more threatening, lofting a pass over the City defence for the run of Diogo Dalot but he cannot quite put the ball under his spell in the penalty area.

Rashford finds himself near the right touchline and finds room to drive inside with the ball, where he is sandwiched between Semenyo and Anderson. Free-kick for United in a crossing position right of centre, and from the second phase a Martinez cross flies into the gloves of Donnarumma.

An early glimpse of United’s slightly flimsy central midfield with Cherki finding space behind them and Enzo Fernandez’s strike from distance deflecting over the bar. Martinez heads Anderson’s delivery behind for another corner.

This time City take it short, but United clear their lines when the ball is crossed into the box.

The ball changes hands in midfield a couple of times in quick succession. Dalot pressing Semenyo but the winger gets away from him, but United win a challenge before Anderson nips in. Promising start if you want aggression and intensity.

Maguire is then penalised for a foul on Cherki in a more promising position for City, but from a free-kick taken short the flag goes up for offside. City claim there was a foul on Cherki from Fernandes.

United get the first Manchester derby of the season under way.

As expected, there is that banner above the mouth of the tunnel.

“THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE” banner is displayed above the Munich tunnel on the south west corner of the Stretford End.

Avram Glazer is in the directors’ box with Sir Jim Ratcliffe behind his co-owner.

"THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE" banner above the tunnel#MUFC pic.twitter.com/hrs71K7r1y

Probably keeping the emotions away, which is not easy. It’s just try to embrace the chaos, that’s it..

We’ve got a lot of encouragement going into the season, of course we wanted more points at this stage. We understand how important this game is and what it can do but it’s getting the balance, we know it’s a long season and we have to be consistent over a period of time. In some ways everything is on today, and it has to be, but it’s not everything in terms of the bigger picture.

Michael Carrick’s record has been outstanding, particularly at Old Trafford. They’ve been brilliant here and very difficult to beat.

If United drop points today, people will say it’s a bad start, if they win today, people will say they’re back.

Dalot did not want to take Carrick’s team selection for granted when talking about the milestone, but United’s manager is not replete with full-back options.

Some supporters also targeted ambitions to build a new 100,000 capacity stadium adjacent to Old Trafford by singing: “You can shove your new ground up your a---.”

Inside Old Trafford, all flags in the Stretford End are set to be removed with and replaced by one banner that reads: “THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE.”

"An absolute WORLDIE from range!"Lewis Dunk scores a contender for goal of the season 🤯 pic.twitter.com/m5bPzm5Wm3

Struck by the nature of both midfields. The other five are not especially adept at covering ground and defensive actions, so this could well be wide open.

Supporters have reacted with outrage to the club’s handling of a controversial anti ticket touting operation they felt unfairly singled out innocent fans.

And thousands have taken to the streets to voice their anger at how they feel they are being treated by the co-owners.

Plumes of red and green and yellow smoke filled the air as fans brandished banners and flags and chanted anti-Glazer and Ratcliffe songs.

Enzo Maresca has selected the more attacking option by playing Enzo Fernandez deeper alongside Elliot Anderson, rather than pushing the Argentine up a line and starting O’Reilly or Bouaddi. Still no Doku for City, and Foden has been preferred to Ndiaye out wide.

It is a very offensive-minded XI with Dorgu at full-back and a midfield trio of Tielemans, Fernandes and Mainoo behind Mbeumo, Cunha and Rashford. The results could be spectacular, but City should fancy punching holes in that set up.

Man Utd XI: Lammens, Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Dorgu, Tielemans, Mainoo, Mbeumo, Cunha, Fernandes, Rashford

They are now 2-0 down against Brighton and Taiwo Awoniyi has been sent off for an elbow. Bar a miracle, it will be zero points from four games for Frank Lampard’s team.

There will be no flags in the Stretford End today in a protest against ticketing policy which United say is about stopping touts, but loyal, innocent fans may have been caught in the crossfire. A crackdown has led to 685 supporters being stripped of their season tickets and another 464 being sanctioned. Fans will unfurl a giant banner reading “The Way You Treat Us Is A Disgrace” aimed at the club’s hierarchy this afternoon. You can read more here from James Ducker.

"You can shove your new ground up your a*rse"#MUFC protests pic.twitter.com/EMmnF8FhNo

Kostoulas has given Brighton the lead away at Coventry, who are still to pick up their first Premier League point. Around five minutes until half-time in that one. It was quite some finish.

"What an outstanding finish, absolutely brilliant!"Charalampos Kostoulas fires Brighton in front with a wonderful finish 💥 pic.twitter.com/bMKJACr2bd

Both of these teams were in Champions League action this week but, as James Ducker explores in this piece, United have missed out in six of the last 13 campaigns. City have been ever-presents, with significant sporting and financial benefits. Over the 10 years between 2016 and 2025, City generated £343m more in broadcast revenue and prize money from European football than their derby rivals.

Sam Wallace was at Carrington this week to speak with Diogo Dalot, the Manchester United right-back who could make his 250th appearance for the club this afternoon. Dalot has been through some tumultuous times at Old Trafford, and is one of the great survivors in the squad. He talks about the scrutiny at United, his musical family and the negatives of social media for young players in an interview you can read here.

My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

To most, it feels like Carrick remains an interim solution in all but name, entrusted with the keys to Old Trafford until a super coach can move in during the summer of 2027. Carrick will not see it that way, of course, but there are certain perceptions which will be tough to shake off.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the season’s first Manchester derby, with midfield rebuilds the theme of the summer on both sides of town.

Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all be involved for City, who lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in the engine room, while United have recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in an attempt to address a long-standing problem.

Rodri’s departure and a Community Shield shellacking by Arsenal prompted some gloomy forecasts for Enzo Maresca and City, but confidence has grown since. The late turnaround at home to Bournemouth on the opening weekend could well look very important in a few months’ time, while Crystal Palace and Coventry have also been put away. Victory in Porto was probably Maresca’s most impressive result to date at City, though winning at Old Trafford would usurp that. Three points for City would mean they join Arsenal on a maximum of 12 points from four games.

It has been a patchy start to the campaign for United and Michael Carrick, and this afternoon’s result will go a long way to shaping perceptions of where they are. The concession of a late equalise at Everton, in addition to a dreadful loss at Hull, adds a degree of pressure. United will be buoyed by their performance in this fixture in January, when they delivered possibly the best performance of the post-Ferguson years to slay City in a 2-0 win that could well have been four or five.

With Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Kobbie Mainoo prominent in midfield, United are trying to shift to a more possession-heavy approach, but any success against City in recent times has tended to come on the counter-attack. Maresca’s team have had lots of the ball in their first few games of the season, so that is the expected pattern again.Full team news on the way later.

#1530. Comparing Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo’s final international stats

A major chapter in the Lionel Messi vs Cristiano Ronaldo rivalry is drawing to a close, with Messi having bade Argentina farewell and Ronaldo having now announced his retirement from international football with Portugal.

With both players’ international careers now over, their total tallies for Portugal and Argentina are finalised. How do they compare on the international stage?

After a legendary career with Argentina, in which he’s comfortably their all-time top goalscorer and appearance-maker, the 39-year-old captain waved goodbye to the fans with a goal and two assists against Benin.

Ronaldo has now confirmed that his time with Portugal is also over, bringing the curtain down on an extraordinary international career. Whether he’ll be given the opportunity to enjoy a farewell appearance in front of his home supporters remains to be seen.

The 41-year-old leaves international football as the most prolific goalscorer in men’s international history, having represented Portugal at five World Cups and six European Championships.

Few players will ever get close to the international numbers Messi and Ronaldo have left behind. Ronaldo finishes with 234 Portugal appearances and 146 goals, both higher than Messi’s final totals of 207 caps and 125 goals for Argentina.

Ronaldo was also the more prolific goalscorer – both in terms of his overall tally and averages. His 146 strikes arrived at one every 127 minutes, compared with Messi’s rate of one every 136. Taking penalties out of the equation leaves Ronaldo ahead again, averaging a goal every 151 minutes to Messi’s 172.

Messi’s advantage comes in the creative department. He provided 67 assists for Argentina, comfortably clear of Ronaldo’s 37, and that swings the overall goal contribution numbers his way: 193 to 183.

There is very little separating them elsewhere. Messi scored 12 direct free-kicks to Ronaldo’s 11 and registered 11 hat-tricks to Ronaldo’s 10. He was also, surprisingly, more reliable from the spot, converting 78% of his penalties compared with Ronaldo’s 69%.

Add everything together, and Messi averaged a goal or assist every 89 minutes of his international career. Ronaldo’s corresponding figure is every 101 minutes, despite his superior individual scoring rate.

Messi also finishes one ahead in the trophy count. Argentina won four major honours during his career, including the World Cup and two Copa Americas, while Ronaldo helped Portugal claim Euro 2016 and two Nations League titles.

Here’s the full breakdown of Messi and Ronaldo’s stats on the international stage:

Appearances: 208 Goals: 126 Assists: 67 ⭐ Goal Contributions: 193 ⭐

Penalties scored/taken: 26/33 ⭐ (78% ⭐) Free-kicks: 12 ⭐ Hat-tricks: 11 ⭐

Minutes per goal: 136.5 Minutes per non-penalty goal: 172.1 Minutes per goal or assist: 89.1 ⭐

1 x FIFA World Cup 1 x Finalissima 2 x Copa America

Appearances: 234 ⭐ Goals: 146 ⭐ Assists: 37 Goal Contributions: 183

Penalties scored/taken: 23/33 (69% ⭐) Free-kicks: 11 Hat-tricks: 10

Minutes per goal: 127 ⭐ Minutes per non-penalty goal: 151 ⭐ Minutes per goal or assist: 101

1 x UEFA European Championship 2 x UEFA Nations League

#1529. Angry Oliver Glasner fumes at 's*** situation' in explosive rant: Nottingham Forest boss warns players they need to change or he'll be sacked and hits out at 'pattern' of problems

Published: 17:24 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 09:37 EDT, 1 November 2026

Nottingham Forest manager Oliver Glasner launched into an extraordinary rant after his team's 2-0 defeat at Brentford on Saturday left them second to bottom of the Premier League.

And Glasner made it clear that if things don't improve he will be sacked, or even walk away from the City Ground job.

Daily Mail Sport understands the under-fire Austrian is not happy with some of his players' attitudes and their response to his work since joining the club from Crystal Palace in the summer.

Glasner revealed that he had refused a request from one of his players to make his own way back to Nottingham from London after the game, banging the table at the press conference when revealing his dismay at the very idea.

'We have to accept it's not good enough,' he said. 'If we lose four of the last five games, it's not good enough. And that's why for me, it's now time that we change things, that I change things, and that's what I will do.

'Everywhere, and I feel I could see a few things from day number one. I feel now maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff, and it's always compromises.

Oliver Glasner made his feelings clear after the final whistle, with Forest in the bottom three

Striker Igor Thiago's goal secured the latest triumph for upwardly-mobile Brentford

'It's a clear way. I will tell [the players] what we want to do, what we have to do, and if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround, and if not, the sixth manager [since the start of last season] will come in.

'But, you know, the players, the staff, they remain in the same situation. And it's the same, sorry for the word, s*** situation that the club had last year.

'So you need to change and rebuild from the bottom to the top. And this is clear for me. And this is what I will do. And without any compromises. Zero. Zero. And if these things don't work, they will let me know [about  my exit].'

The Bees had taken the lead after half an hour when Nikola Milenkovic steered the ball past his own goalkeeper. Igor Thiago continued his return to form as his second-half strike helped Brentford end their five-game wait for a win against the Midlands side.

For Glasner, it was all too much. 'I didn't come to Nottingham because I was bored at home,' he went on. 'No, I came to Nottingham to succeed. I came to Nottingham to get the visions of the owner and the fans and the club to reality. And therefore we need to have a bigger change than maybe I thought, to be honest.

'But again, when you're in a club, then you see what's going on. And I'm desperate to get this tournament around.

'But again, Oliver Glasner can't do anything alone. And I said this so often, and not just after a defeat. I always said the same after winning.

'It's not me, no, but we're all together and can do it. But I know where we have to go. And therefore, it's exactly this, being ruthless. And either you buy in or you leave. It's the only way.

'There is no compromise. Either you buy in where we want to go as a club. Because, and I mentioned it, if you're three times struggling, four or five Premier League seasons, struggling, being at the bottom of the league, there is a pattern.

'And I just know that Oliver Glasner is not here for five years. You see my mood, right? So, yes (I understand fans’ boos).

'And again, that's what should be expected. They say, hey, yes, we are nice. I paid the train ticket and the ticket here.

'And then, yeah, we're the same again. I think it's not, again, it's not a lack of effort, but there are a few things very obvious. And it's, let's say, we're talking about the realities.

'We are outrun by the opposition in every single game to change it. And if you can't change it, we need different personnel. And if the club doesn't want to change it, they need a different manager. I'm desperate to change it. Desperate.'

#1528. When will Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo retire from professional football?

When will Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo bring the curtains down on their careers? The end is nigh for both.

They once ruled the footballing world as the best players of their generation. Their legacies remain strong as two of the best players of all time. The GOAT debates are endless.

But time catches up with everyone and the end is near for Messi’s and Ronaldo’s legendary careers. The question is: how much longer do we have left to enjoy them?

Ronaldo is the older of the pair at 41. Messi recently turned 39. Neither are playing in Europe anymore, of course, with Ronaldo in the Saudi Pro League and Messi in MLS.

Both have now brought their international careers to an end, with Messi having already said goodbye to Argentina and Ronaldo having announced his retirement from Portugal.

Ronaldo’s latest announcement represents a significant milestone in the winding down of his career, although he has yet to confirm whether he’ll play in one last farewell match.

At club level, both players still have time left on their contracts. Ronaldo’s deal with Al-Nassr is due to last until the end of the season. Messi, meanwhile, has a contract until December 2028 with Inter Miami.

Per some reports from when he signed his latest renewal in 2025, Ronaldo’s contract contains an option to extend into the summer of 2028 as well.

Thus, there could be another couple of years left of Messi and Ronaldo as professional footballers.

But contracts aren’t always fulfilled and many factors could influence each player’s future. We just hope injury isn’t the way either go out.

The less outspoken of the two long-time Ballon d’Or rivals, Messi hasn’t given too much away about his future in club football.

“I know that the moment I feel that I am no longer able to perform, that I no longer enjoy or help my team-mates, I will quit,” he offered in March 2024.

“I’m very self-critical. I know when I’m good, when I’m bad, when I’m playing well, and when I’m playing badly.

“When I feel it’s time to take that step, I’ll take it without thinking about age. If I feel good, I’ll always try to keep competing because it’s what I like and what I know how to do.

“I haven’t yet thought of what I’m going to do when I retire. Today, I try to enjoy the day-to-day, the moments, without thinking about life after [football].”

However, the sad news of his father passing away prompted Messi to give a rare update on his future this summer.

“I don’t know how to carry on. I used to just play football, and now I’m really not sure if I’ll carry on doing it for much longer,” he posted on social media.

“You were by my side from the very beginning. We were so close to the end. Why didn’t you hang in there just a little longer so we could finish this together?”

Reflecting on the World Cup after Argentina lost the final to Spain, Messi added: “I wanted to win it so I could bring the trophy to you and show you a new one. I couldn’t, my legs had nothing left. This time I tried to push past my physical limits, but I couldn’t. I never managed to feel right.”

And since, Messi has confirmed he is bowing out from international duty altogether.

He posted on Instagram on August 31: “After the time that has passed since the final, and after giving it a lot of thought, I want to let everyone know that I am retiring from the National Team…

“It was a decision that hurt—and still hurts deep down—but I understand that the time has come. I swear to you that I always gave it my all—not just in these last few years when we won everything, but before that too; I always fought and left everything on the field for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you feel proud to be Argentine through football.

“Time is running short, chapters come to a close, and this is one that hurts me deeply. I love, have loved, and will always love being part of the National Team. I’ve given everything I had; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are some great young players coming up who deserve to be here.

“Thank you for all the affection over these past 20 years. I will miss hearing you from the pitch so much. Now I’ll be just one of you, cheering and supporting from the outside (through the good times and the bad—especially the bad).

“Thank you to my family for always being there, for accompanying me on this journey—so beautiful, yet so difficult. Thank you to every coach, teammate, and official I’ve shared this path with. I take with me unforgettable memories and moments.

“I leave with the peace of mind and pride of having given you—alongside my teammates—moments we once only dreamed of. It was an incredible experience to live this with you all. I love you!

“Thank you, God, for making me Argentine.

“*I wrote these words on July 21st, two days after the final. Today, after what happened with my dad, I am even more convinced than before.”

And so that’s the end of Messi’s international career, after 207 caps, 125 goals, 68 assists, two Copa Americas and a World Cup.

Ronaldo has been more vocal about the end of his career, partially because of his personality and partially because it’s probably closer.

He hinted in November 2025 that he could retire ‘soon’, before clarifying: “Soon for me means in 10 years… No, I’m joking.

“I’m really enjoying the moment right now. As you know, in football, when you reach some age, you count the months very quick.

“I feel very good in this moment. I score goals, I still feel quick and sharp. I’m enjoying my game in the national team. But of course, let’s be honest. What I mean by soon is probably one or two years.”

He has also confirmed his ongoing pursuit of reaching 1000 career goals will have an impact on when he calls it quits.

“It’s hard to continue playing, but I am motivated,” he said in December.

“My passion is high and I want to continue. It doesn’t matter where I play, whether in the Middle East or Europe. I always enjoy playing football and I want to keep going.

“You know what my goal is. I want to win trophies and I want to reach that number [1000 goals] that you all know. I will reach the number for sure, if no injuries.”

For what it’s worth, Messi could be capable of reaching 1000 goals as well, but it remains to be seen if that will have a bearing on his future.

Ronaldo’s international future, meanwhile, has now been settled. Having previously suggested that he would reflect on his Portugal career after the World Cup, the five-time Ballon d’Or winner has officially announced his retirement from international football.

He made the announcement in a heartfelt farewell message to the Portuguese people, opening with the words: “Portugal will always be a part of me.”

“The time has come to hang up our national team’s number 7 shirt. I never felt it was mine alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and responsibility of wearing it and defending it in stadiums all around the world,” Ronaldo wrote.

The 41-year-old admitted that the decision was difficult, adding: “Today, the time has come to hand it over, but it was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made alone.”

Ronaldo’s international career therefore comes to an end after 234 appearances and 146 goals for Portugal, having helped his country win Euro 2016 and two Nations League titles.

That leaves his club future as the biggest remaining question. Ronaldo has made no announcement about retiring from football altogether, and his pursuit of 1000 career goals remains a significant motivation.

His current contract with Al-Nassr expires at the end of the season, by which point he’ll be 42. Every chance he calls it quits then if he scores his thousandth goal before then, which appears likely.

#1527. Didier Deschamps, the official announcement

The dream of Fenerbahçe supporters has passed. After the announcement of Ismail Kartal’s departure, many were hoping for the arrival of a big name to manage a complicated locker room. Arne Slot, Pep Guardiola and Julian Nagelsmann were thus cited.

Just like Didier Deschamps, who has definitely made many supporters dream since he left the bench of the France team. The aura of the 1998 and 2018 world champion arouses real expectations, and his profile as a leader of men is hoped for in the four corners of Europe. In addition to Turkey, where his name had already been mentioned after the departure of former coach Vincenzo Montella, Didier Deschamps is also mentioned with insistence on the side of Manchester United, where the future of Michael Carrick no longer seems to hang by a thread. At Old Trafford, his ability to impose iron discipline and his winning culture are seen by many as the ideal remedy for Mancunian turbulence.

But it is also on the side of Juventus Turin that the name of the French technician makes hearts beat. Many fans of the Old Lady dream of her big return to the Piedmontese bench. Having passed through the club as a player before being the coach during the rise to Serie A in 2006-2007, Deschamps maintains his rating intact in Piedmont, where his tactical pragmatism and his history with the Bianconeri make him the perfect candidate to rekindle the Turin flame.

In Istanbul, the name Didier Deschamps had all the makings of wishful thinking. To save an increasingly chaotic season, the Istanbul management chose familiarity and pragmatism by formalizing the appointment of Emre Belözoğlu as coach. The 46-year-old former Turkish international, who was a professional player for 24 years, is making his comeback to the very first club he coached just after hanging up his boots.

This return to basics recalls a situation well known to yellow and blue supporters. In 2021, the club management had already urgently called on him to take the reins of the first team following the departure of Erol Bulut. At the time, Belözoğlu was able to respond with a very honorable record to end the season: 7 victories, 2 draws and only one defeat. Despite this remarkable recovery, the club’s staff chose to hire Vitor Pereira to launch the following campaign, encouraging the Turkish technician to continue his coaching career elsewhere.

This new appointment above all illustrates the extreme instability which currently reigns within the Istanbul institution. This is in fact the fifth change of coach at Fenerbahçe during the year 2026 alone. Belözoğlu succeeds the Dutchman Dirk Kuyt, who was appointed interim coach on October 28 following the resignation of Ismail Kartal, caused by a particularly bitter defeat in the derby against sworn rival Galatasaray (1-2).

For the man who wore the Fenerbahçe tunic 227 times during his playing career, the challenge promises to be immense even if the prestigious victory won on Wednesday against Liverpool in the Champions League brings hope.

“To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team.

“I never it belonged to me alone. But for 23 years I had the privilege and responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums.

There is the question of whether Ronaldo will play one final match for the team, having last featured against Norway in September. Neither player nor team has confirmed whether he is finished now or in the near future with Portugal’s next game being a Nations League tie against Denmark on November 14.

In a statement, the Portuguese national team hinted at a final match by promising a “due tribute.”

“The Portuguese Football Federation expresses its deepest and most enduring gratitude to its eternal captain, Cristiano Ronaldo, who today announced his definitive retirement from the National Team.

#1524. Doubts had been gathering about Roberto De Zerbi but not now, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI, as Crystal Palace's ludicrous acts of self-sabotage prove costly in 2-0 defeat

By RIATH AL-SAMARRAI, CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 15:56 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 10:07 EDT, 1 November 2026

For the first time in 616 days, Tottenham have won three games in succession. If that proves Roberto De Zerbi’s prowess over at least two of his predecessors, then he will presumably reserve some thanks to the assistance of Crystal Palace.

On a night when Palace crossed to the north of London, with their manager in grave danger of the sack, they contrived to commit an utterly ludicrous act of self-sabotage in two phases.

The first defined the match, with Jean-Philippe Mateta dismissed after only 13 minutes for a challenge that was as brainless as it was dangerous.

From there, Pierre Sage’s side quickly conceded from a set-piece with the sort of defending that explained why Palace have shipped more goals than any other team in the top flight. That no further damage was inflicted until Jan Paul van Hecke’s second-half header was less reflective of the game than the tally showing 34 Tottenham shots to Palace’s two.

Given Sage’s tenuous grip on his job, and the thunderous face in the crowd of his chairman, Steve Parish, that might prove to be the final straw. If it is, Mateta should at least have the decency to drive him to the airport.

Sage said: ‘I am responsible. I have to find solutions. They have to trust in me because I will give my life for it. If I have one hour or 10 years, I will try my best.’

Archie Gray opened the scoring for Tottenham after 25 minutes to settle the nerves

Jan Paul van Hecke slid in to make it 2-0 and all but wrap the game up for the home team

In the recent past, such doubts were gathering around De Zerbi, but not now, and especially with a favourable run of fixtures on the horizon. Having belatedly entered the top half of the table, his side are finally aligning results with performances, even if this fourth game in an unbeaten stretch was aided so much by the opposition.

There remains an issue with chance conversion – both Dominic Solanke and Omar Marmoush were underwhelming here, with the slight mitigation that Palace spent the better part of 75 minutes camped on the edge of their own area. Marmoush, who started at No 10 after earlier games on the left and up front, appears no closer to revealing his best position.

De Zerbi’s solution was to direct traffic to the wings and it worked a treat. Mathys Tel, riding the isolated high of his performance against Chelsea, was again sharp. So too Mohammed Kudus. But the real gains for Tottenham in this purple patch have come from the central pairing of Sandro Tonali and Matheus Fernandes.

They cost a fortune to acquire and have taken their sweet time to gel, but that partnership has developed to strong effect. On the ball, they are the tempo setters, and off it they have shaped the press that is key to De Zerbi’s system. They controlled this game.

‘Tonali was unbelievable,’ said De Zerbi. ‘We played with two players more - Tonali (counted) double.’

He added: ‘I am very happy with the performance. (But) if we want perfection we have to be more nasty. If I am No 9 or No 10 I want to score.’

The last sentence is very much the Tottenham riddle – an inability to finish what they start. But those frustrations are now coming from an upwardly mobile situation.

Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi is banishing the doubters as his team climb the table

Having belatedly entered the top half of the table, Spurs are finally aligning results with performances

For Sage, along with whatever consequences this result brings, the regret will come from knowing his side had looked decent out of the gate.

But the red card eradicated those traces of momentum. Initially, referee Michael Oliver felt a booking was sufficient for Mateta’s studs-up lunge into Micky van de Ven’s ankle, but the VAR suggested an upgrade. On review, Oliver agreed.

Sage’s reaction? He had a look of pure deflation. The tackle was bad enough but the need to make it was non-existent – Mateta was chasing a losing cause in Tottenham’s half against one of the quickest defenders in the league. Dismal.

Naturally, it shifted the game in Tottenham’s favour, if only to the effect of a one-goal lead by the break. As with Mateta’s dismissal, the Spurs breakthrough was avoidable for Palace, with Gray left unmarked at the far post before planting his head on Kudus’s high, looping corner.

The video analysis will do Sage no favours. Kudus’s delivery was excellent, that much is true, but five Tottenham men had gathered at the far post with only three markers – even factoring for the red card, the tracking of Gray was abysmal.

At half-time, De Zerbi substituted Gray, who was carrying a yellow card, and Spurs maintained momentum by creating openings for Tel, Matheus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke and Solanke.

Palace were being pummelled but survived until Van Hecke’s finish for 2-0. As with the Chelsea win, Fernandes stood out in its creation with an excellent cross, from which Van Hecke powered a header at Dean Henderson.

The initial save was good, but the ball returned to Van Hecke, who was sat on his backside and able to steer his second header past Henderson. Sage could use similar inspiration from the floor.

#1523. When will Cristiano Ronaldo score goal No. 1000 after international retirement announcement?

Cristiano Ronaldo is now just 15 goals away from reaching 1,000 goals, the landmark he has openly targeted as the defining achievement of the last years of his career. It now becomes his final challenge following his announcement that he’ll retire from the Portugal national team.

At 41, the question is no longer whether Ronaldo can reach the four-figure mark. It is how long it will take him to get there.

The Portuguese superstar remains prolific for Al-Nassr, having taken his tally to 985 with a hat-trick in a 5-3 victory over Al Kholood on October 29th

He’s now confirmed that his 23-year international career is over, announcing his decision in an emotional farewell message to Portugal’s supporters.

“The time has come to hang up our national team’s number 7 shirt,” Ronaldo wrote, admitting that it had not been an easy decision.

That leaves Al-Nassr as his only remaining route to the 1,000-goal milestone, barring any change of heart over his international retirement or a farewell appearance for Portugal.

We’ve crunched the numbers and mapped out the various scenarios.

“I want to reach 1,000 goals,” Ronaldo said, unveiling his last major career ambition on Rio Ferdinand’s YouTube channel just over two years ago.

“If I don’t have any injuries, this for me is the most important [thing], I want that. For me, the best mark that I can have in football is to reach, first, 900 goals. After, my challenge is to be at 1,000 goals.

“All the goals I have scored, they have video. They all have video. Listen, I respect all of them [Pele and Di Stefano]. And if you want more goals, I can bring them from training, too. And I will prove to the people after. They prefer this player, or this is the best one. I don’t care about that.”

Ronaldo has maintained the importance of that ambition, previously identifying it alongside winning another Nations League title as a major motivation. The latter is now off the table, but his pursuit of four figures remains very much alive.

“One thousand goals, yes, and the national team. Winning the Nations League, the competition starts tomorrow [Thursday], it’s a new age.”

With all that in mind, here’s our calculations for when Ronaldo could potentially reach the milestone of 1000 goals in his professional career.

– Barring any major career-ending injuries, Ronaldo still looks likely to reach the milestone of a thousand goals at some point in 2027. Possibly as early as January or February, particularly if he maintains his recent scoring form.

– It’s possible that if Ronaldo enjoys a resurgence and goes on a hot streak akin to his most prolific peak at Real Madrid, he could do it before the end of the year, and his latest hat-trick suggests that isn’t entirely out of the question. He would still need 15 goals in little over two months, though.

– If you take his recent rate of scoring (27 goals in 42 appearances during the calendar year of 2026) as what he’ll likely maintain, another 24 appearances would be required to score the remaining 15 goals. That would take us through to around February or March 2027. Crucially, that calculation previously allowed for further Portugal appearances, which can no longer be taken for granted.

– There is an argument that Ronaldo could be set to improve upon that scoring rate. He’s been written off on the international stage after poor showings in the last two major summer tournaments, but he scored eight goals in nine games in the 2024-25 Nations League and a further five goals in qualifying for the 2026 World Cup. Although his international career is now over, rediscover that form in the Saudi Pro League, up his rate to around 1.00 goals per game and fill his boots for Al-Nassr, and Ronaldo could conceivably reach four figures early in 2027. At that rate, he’d need just 15 more appearances.

– There is a counter-argument that Ronaldo will instead slow down in these final furlongs of his career. There had been signs of that earlier in the season, but his hat-trick against Al Kholood was a timely reminder of his enduring goalscoring prowess. His 27 goals in 42 appearances in 2026 work out at 0.64 goals per game. Maintain that rate, and he’ll need another 24 games to score the 15 goals required to reach number one thousand. That should be comfortably achievable before the end of Al-Nassr’s 2026-27 campaign, which is due to end in late May 2027.

– The biggest unknown is now how prolific Ronaldo can remain at club level. His international retirement means he’ll no longer have the opportunity to add goals in Portugal colours, although it should also give him more time to concentrate on Al-Nassr and potentially manage his workload. Whether that makes him even more prolific in Saudi Arabia is another matter.

– What kind of form he’ll show to get there is ultimately anyone’s guess. His latest hat-trick against Al Kholood, following a quieter couple of outings against Neom SC and Al Faysaly, suggests he’s still capable of producing spectacular goalscoring performances for Al-Nassr. But the end of his international career removes one variable from our projections, while leaving the exact date far from certain.

– We’ll hedge our bets and estimate that Ronaldo’s form over the coming months will be somewhere between his spectacular peak and a severe decline. He is playing in the Saudi Pro League, after all, and his team is set up to feed him chances. With no more international fixtures to factor into the equation, we’re backing him to keep ticking along for Al-Nassr. With just 15 goals left to score, and his recent hat-trick suggesting he’s finding his rhythm again, we’re sticking with February 2027 as our tentative prediction for Ronaldo’s 1,000th career goal, although the loss of potential Portugal appearances could yet push that date back.

#1521. Can you name Portugal’s XI from Cristiano Ronaldo’s competitive debut, 2004?

Cristiano Ronaldo is the all-time top scorer in the history of international football, but he took a while to get going with Portugal. How well do you remember his early days?

Luiz Felipe Scolari handed the then-teenage Manchester United winger his debut off the bench in a 1-0 friendly victory over Kazakhstan in September 2003, and he went on to make a handful more cameo appearances in friendlies as Portugal geared up for hosting Euro 2004.

His first competitive appearance didn’t come until the opening match of that home tournament, however.

Greece beat Portugal 2-1 in that opening game and would famously go on to beat them once again in the final to lift the first international trophy in their history.

Ronaldo was introduced at half-time by his Brazilian manager and scored his first goal for Portugal in injury time, but as Greece were already 2-0 up it was only a consolation.
